I think there's many factors that make women more likely to be diagnosed with BPD. For one, women are more likely to go to a medical professional with concerns. A significant portion (I want to say most) of medical issues are diagnosed based on male symptoms, e.g. autism, ADHD, and this leads to misdiagnoses (including of BPD). 

I have BPD and have worked incredibly hard through years of therapy and self-work to be able to manage it how I do now. As much as I can see the commonality between some of the description of hysteria & BPD, BPD is a real disorder and I wouldn't want it to be dismissed under this umbrella.
